message: Trigger-produced fact changes must drive subsequent deferred trigger batches. Phase 8 writes trigger effects to beliefs without recording their keys and then clears the entire changed-fact set, so a trigger A that sets y cannot cause trigger B depending on y to fire on the next tick.

Scenario initial beliefs must be visible to newly installed trigger rules. loadScenario injects initial beliefs and registers triggers but never seeds changedFacts; a trigger already satisfied by those initial facts is skipped in all batches until a dialogue explicitly re-writes a dependency.

TriggerRule.then accepts the full Effect union and should execute its declared effects. Phase 8 supports only set_fact and discards every other legal Effect with a warning, despite the DSL allowing give, take, damage and register_trigger effects in then arrays.

The target field on set_fact identifies the agent whose belief is changed. Trigger execution resolves rule.targets but completely ignores effect.target, writing every set_fact to each rule target. A rule targeting agent a with setFact('b', 'alert', true) modifies a rather than b.
Trigger effects must activate dependent rules in a subsequent deferred batch. Phase 8 writes beliefs without recording changed keys and clears the batch, so chained triggers never run.
Scenario triggers execute the effects accepted by the DSL and Effect union. Phase 8 silently skips all trigger effects other than set_fact.
AgentRef on set_fact specifies its recipient. Trigger execution ignores effect.target and sets every rule target's belief instead.

iOS API-key destination creation must be usable non-interactively with CLI options. appleApiKeyId is declared as an undefined local rather than a CLI option, so API-key destination creation always exits in non-interactive mode after uploading the key.

iOS API-key destination creation must work non-interactively with CLI options. appleApiKeyId is initialized to undefined instead of being accepted as an option, so every non-interactive API-key creation uploads a key then exits at the mandatory key-ID check.

Name searches must find existing files/folders before reporting absence or creating a replacement. Both name searches omit nextPageToken and treat an empty first files.list page as definitive absence, although Drive may return empty intermediate pages.

API quota exhaustion must be distinguished from insufficient permissions. parseDriveError does not recognize Drive's 403 dailyLimitExceeded API-quota reason and returns DrivePermissionError for the standard Daily Limit Exceeded message.

Name searches must find existing appData files and folders before returning not-found or creating a folder. Both name searches discard nextPageToken and treat an empty first page as definitive absence, although Drive files.list can return empty partial pages with a continuation token.

API quota errors must be represented as DriveQuotaExceededError rather than permission errors. The 403 quota reason allowlist omits dailyLimitExceeded and storageQuotaExceeded; responses with these reasons and ordinary messages such as 'Daily Limit Exceeded' or 'The user's Drive storage quota has been exceeded' become DrivePermissionError.

A completed NOT_BUILT build must publish a terminal status, using WARNING when SKIPPED support cannot be established. The new mandatory version lookup aborts NOT_BUILT notifications if /version fails; there is no conservative fallback to WARNING.

NOT_BUILT must still publish a terminal commit status when skipped support cannot be determined. The newly required version request can fail independently of the commit-status endpoint; its IOException aborts the notification instead of falling back to WARNING, leaving the previous pending status in place.

API key management must not disclose generated or listed credentials to diagnostic logs. The new API-key endpoints use requestV3, which logs the entire parsed response when debug is enabled, including data.key and every key in the list.

API key management must not disclose credential values through SDK diagnostic logging. The new listApiKeys and createApiKey methods route secret-bearing responses through requestV3, which logs the full response object to console when debug is enabled, exposing API key values.
